equivalents.note: The Tibetan does not transliterate the rāga name but translates it as if it were kāmada, 'dod pa sbyin pa 'giving what is desired', an ordinary phrase that could occur elsewhere in another sense.
The Tibetan has no word for a conduit: pad+mar 'bab pa'i chu, 'the water flowing into the lotus', seems to render bahai paṇālem̐ together, turning the channel into the water it carries.
tshogs pa, 'gathering, assembly', takes melem̐ as a meeting or gathering rather than a union, and the same word renders sandoha 'mass' in cp.27.m2 (dga' ba la sogs pa'i tshogs pas).
Munidatta's prajñopāyamelake appears as thabs dang shes rab sbyor bas, 'by the joining of means and wisdom', a different word from the verse's tshogs pa.
Where the Bengali has an instrumental noun (lolem̐, 'in play'), the Tibetan makes rol the finite verb of the line: bde ba chen por rol, '(he) revels in great bliss'.
The Sanskrit līlayāvagataṃ, 'understood in play', becomes khong du chud pas rol pa'o, 'having understood, he revels', so play is the result of the understanding rather than its manner.
bzhi is the cardinal 'four' (the ordinal would be bzhi pa), so nam phyed kyi thun mtshams bzhi la can also be read 'at the four junctures of midnight' rather than 'at midnight, the fourth juncture'.

The Tibetan transliterates the name instead of using the usual Tibetan brkyang ma; the preceding byang chub kyi sems 'bab pa la la nA could also be parsed with a dative la, leaving a shortened la nA, but the sense is the same.
The Tibetan transliterates the name instead of using the usual Tibetan ro ma.
de nyid here renders tattva in bla ma dam pa'i gsung gi de nyid rin po che, but the same words serve throughout as the plain emphatic 'that very' (don de nyid for tam evārthaṃ in cp.27.m1 and m4–m5).
The Tibetan reads anadhigatatattvānām as de nyid rnams kyi ma rig pa, 'not understanding the realities', so what has no room here is ignorance of reality rather than people who have not grasped it.
In Kāṇha's quoted line the Tibetan turns the noun bandhana into a verb: rab tu 'bab pas rang sems 'ching, 'by flowing forth it binds one's own mind'.
The Tibetan has bla ma'i drin gyis, 'by the guru's kindness', the phrase it uses for guruprasāda in cp.27.m5, so it reads the lineage as the guru's grace rather than a transmission.

questions: nadi at cp.27.m2: the Tibetan has no word for nāḍikā. It reads sum cu rtsa gnyis byang chub kyi sems 'bab pa, 'the thirty-two that carry bodhicitta'; the rtsa there is the numeral connective of sum cu rtsa gnyis ('thirty-two'), not rtsa 'channel', so I give no equivalent.

sahajananda at cp.27.m1: the Tibetan has lhan cig skyes pa'i ros yongs su gang ba, 'wholly filled with the taste of the innate', with no dga' ba. It renders sahajarasa and leaves ānanda out, so there is no word for the full term in this segment. It is matched in cp.27.5b, m3 and m6.
marga: the pack does not list it for cp.27.2a, but the verse's māge (a form the glossary records) is rendered there by lam (ri bong 'dzin lam), so I give that verse line as well as cp.27.m3.
